title: Compute basin entropy — basin_entropy
text: Mathematical background: basin entropy, introduced Daza et al. (2016), measures unpredictability dynamical system's final state given uncertainty initial condition. grid divided boxes size \(\epsilon\), entropy box \(\) : $$S_i = -\sum_{j=1}^{N_A} p_{ij} \log_b(p_{ij})$$ \(p_{ij}\) fraction box \(\) belonging basin \(j\), \(N_A\) number attractors, \(b\) logarithm base. total basin entropy average boxes: $$S_b = \frac{1}{N_{box}} \sum_{=1}^{N_{box}} S_i$$ Interpretation: \(S_b = 0\): boxes monochromatic (uncertainty) \(S_b = \log_b(N_A)\): Maximum uncertainty (uniform distribution boxes) Wada basins, \(S_b\) approaches \(\log_b(N_A)\) boundary, boundary boxes contain \(N_A\) basins fine scales. Small changes initial conditions can lead completely different community compositions. 5-species scenario: Five species compete 3 resources, producing two possible outcomes: Outcome 1: Species {1, 2, 3} survive Outcome 2: Species {1, 4, 5} survive basin boundary outcomes fractal. 8-species scenario: Eight species compete, species 6, 7, 8 invading \(t = 1000\) days. produces three distinct outcomes based invader dominates: Outcome 1: Species 6 dominates Outcome 2: Species 7 dominates Outcome 3: Species 8 dominates 3+ outcomes, system can exhibit Wada basin boundaries.

title: Detect Wada basins using the grid method — wada_grid_method
text: Mathematical background: Consider dynamical system \(N_A \geq 3\) attractors. initial condition \(\mathbf{x}_0\) belongs exactly one basin attraction \(B_k\), \(k = 1, \ldots, N_A\). basins Wada property every point boundary one basin simultaneously boundary basins: $$\partial B_1 = \partial B_2 = \cdots = \partial B_{N_A}$$ grid method algorithm: grid \(n \times n\) boxes, define box \(B_i\): $$m_i = \text{number distinct basins neighborhood } B_i$$ algorithm proceeds follows: Classify grid box number distinct basins 8-connected neighborhood (Moore neighborhood) Identify boundary boxes \(1 < m_i < N_A\) boundary box, construct segment nearest box different basin Apply bisection refinement find additional basins along segment Update \(m_i\) based discovered basins Classification statistics: algorithm computes: $$G_m = |\{: m_i = m\}| \quad \text{(number boxes bordering } m \text{ basins)}$$ $$W_m = \frac{G_m}{\sum_{j>1} G_j} \quad \text{(proportion boundary boxes)}$$ Wada criterion: basin classified Wada \(W_{N_A} \approx 1\), meaning boundary boxes border \(N_A\) basins. implementation uses: $$\text{\_wada} = (W_{N_A} > 1 - \text{tolerance})$$ Computational complexity warning: grid method runtime depends number boundary boxes refinement depth. high-resolution grids (>400x400) many boundary points, computation can slow. parameter max_refinements controls maximum bisection depth; reducing speeds computation cost accuracy. Recommendations: Use max_refinements = 10 quick screening Use max_refinements = 20 (default) accurate results large grids, consider using wada_merging_method first quick screening

title: Detect Wada basins using the merging method — wada_merging_method
text: Mathematical background: Consider dynamical system \(N_A\) basins attraction \(B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_{N_A}\). Wada property states : $$\partial B_1 = \partial B_2 = \cdots = \partial B_{N_A}$$ key insight basins Wada property, merging subset basins change common boundary. Specifically, basin \(B_i\), define merged basin: $$M_i = \bigcup_{j \neq } B_j$$ boundary \(B_i\) \(M_i\) called slim boundary. Wada basins, slim boundaries identical: $$\partial(B_1, M_1) = \partial(B_2, M_2) = \cdots = \partial(B_{N_A}, M_{N_A})$$ merging algorithm: basin \(B_i\) (\(= 1, \ldots, N_A\)): Merge basins \(M_i\) Extract slim boundary \(\partial_i\) \(B_i\) \(M_i\) Compute Hausdorff distance pairs slim boundaries Analyze distance matrix determine Wada property Hausdorff distance: Hausdorff distance point sets \(X\) \(Y\) : $$d_H(X, Y) = \max\{\sup_{x \X} d(x, Y), \sup_{y \Y} d(y, X)\}$$ \(d(x, Y) = \inf_{y \Y} \|x - y\|\) distance point \(x\) set \(Y\). Wada criterion: basins classified Wada : relative difference \((d_{\max} - d_{\min}) / d_{\min} < 2\) maximum distance normalized phase space size \(d_{\max} / L < 0.05\) thresholds empirically calibrated original paper.

title: Detect Wada basins using the saddle-straddle method — wada_straddle_method
text: Mathematical background: dissipative dynamical systems \(N_A \geq 3\) coexisting attractors, basin boundaries contain chaotic saddle \(S\)—invariant set trajectories exhibit chaotic behavior eventually escaping attractor. Wada property implies single connected chaotic saddle lying basin boundaries simultaneously: $$S = S_1 = S_2 = \cdots = S_{N_A}$$ \(S_i\) chaotic saddle boundary basin \(B_i\) merged basin \(M_i = \bigcup_{j \neq } B_j\). saddle-straddle algorithm: algorithm approximates chaotic saddle : Find segment straddling boundary (endpoints different basins) Use bisection refinement segment length \(< \varepsilon\) Record midpoint (approximately saddle) Iterate endpoints forward time (segment expands along unstable manifold saddle) segment length exceeds threshold, refine repeat Continue desired number saddle points collected key insight points chaotic saddle repel trajectories exponentially fast along unstable manifold, causing straddling segment stretch. Repeated bisection converges saddle. Wada criterion: Compute Hausdorff distance pairs computed saddles. basins Wada : $$d_H(S_i, S_j) \ll \text{diam}(S)$$ \(\text{diam}(S)\) diameter saddle set. implementation uses threshold \(d_H < 0.01 \cdot \text{diam}\). Computational complexity warning: computationally expensive Wada detection method. \(N_A\) merged basin pairs, algorithm must: Find initial straddling points (random sampling) Integrate two trajectories forward collecting saddle points Perform repeated bisection refinements total number ODE integration steps scales approximately : $$O(N_A \times n\_points \times T/\Delta t)$$ 3 basins n_points=10000, can take several minutes hours. Recommendations: Use n_points = 1000-2000 exploration Increase n_points = 5000-10000 accurate saddle approximation Use wada_grid_method wada_merging_method faster Wada detection; use method dynamical insight needed
